_what_this_is: THE STACK-SPECIFIC HALF OF THE HARNESS, in one file.
`ci.py` is the step ladder: run each rung in order, print a positive marker with
a count, name the rung that stopped the run. That part IS the same in every
factory. What is NOT the same is every command it runs, so the commands live
here instead of in the ladder.
Set what you have. Leave a step empty and it is SKIPPED LOUDLY -- the log says
<STEP>_SKIPPED and the gate can be told to require the marker, so a skipped rung
is never mistaken for a passed one.
_static_note: Six signals, because each is blind somewhere. typecheck: apps/web/src + packages/*/src only (allowJs is false, so the 49k-line services/api/server.js is invisible). check:syntax: `node --check` over every service file -- parser only. typecheck:api: checkJs over services/api/src behind a ratchet in .factory/locks/api-typecheck-baseline.json, so the ~600 pre-existing errors do not block a merge but new ones do. check:i18n: every dictionary entry in apps/web/src/i18n.ts carries zh, vi and en. check:auth-order: guarded routes declared above their authenticateJWT mount answer 401 to valid tokens; 24 are stranded today (gate at server.js:16658; earlier editions counted everything above the bare mount at ~34060 and over-counted by 10x) and the count is ratcheted so it cannot grow. check:migrations: database/migrations/ is append-only and prefixes are unique; 44 prefixes already collide (110 files), so those are baselined per prefix and one more file on a colliding number fails.

_picking_drift_note: The tenth signal. Nine of them are blind to this one class of fault because they all inspect CODE; this inspects DATA. Picking currently has two write surfaces that are NOT synced: `/api/wms/picking-orders/:id/*` writes canonical `wms_picking_orders`, `/rjvn-picking/:id/*` writes the `rjvn_picking_order` mirror, and `picking_order` is NOT one of migration 309's seven projection-trigger pairs -- so a write through either surface is invisible to the other and no static gate can notice. During slice-1 verification the legacy write happened to be rejected by its own state guard (拣货单状态不允许审批), which is luck, not design. This checker compares status and pick/actual/received quantities across the `rjvn_id` crosswalk and fails on disagreement. It exits 0 (with a printed SKIP) when there is no database, no mirror layer, or the database is unreachable, because an unreachable store cannot prove drift -- so it belongs in the shared rung without going flaky. It deliberately does NOT resolve the stock-invariant question that blocks retiring the mirror surface: reference 拣货出库 decrements on-hand `rjvn_inventory.quantity`, canonical PICK decrements `material_lots.reserved_qty` (server.js:19513) and leaves on-hand alone. Those are different accounting acts; picking one is a business decision, see docs/WMS-ONE-PARITY.md §7.
_route_census_note: The seventh signal, and the only one that exists for a refactor that has not happened yet: 2,726 route registrations across 154 first-segment prefixes (server.js + services/api/src/**/*.js). It fails when the total or any prefix SHRINKS, so moving a route group out of server.js is safe to attempt and a dropped registration is loud. Counts the whole tree on purpose -- a census of server.js alone would block the very split it protects.
_route_shadowing_note: The eighth signal, and the one the seventh cannot see. check:route-census proves no registration was LOST; this proves none of them became UNREACHABLE. `const api = express.Router()` (server.js:117) is mounted by `app.use("/api", api)` at server.js:9368, so a path registered on that router answers before an app-level `app.get("/api/...", requirePermission(...))` declared lower down -- the guard exists, reads as enforcement, and never runs. 10 such guards exist today, all /api/lifecycle/*, baselined in .factory/locks/route-shadowing-baseline.json so a builder cannot add one in the pull request that adds the route. Verified live: a station token without wms.read gets 200 from /api/lifecycle/lots, /summary and /openings (router copies, unguarded) and 403 from /api/lifecycle/exempt-lots, which has no twin.
_register_deps_note: The ninth signal, and the one that would have caught my own worst mistake in this repo. Moving the cycle-count routes out passed `getCurrentUser` into registerCountRoutes; no such function existed in server.js, the identifier was evaluated at module load, and the API threw ReferenceError before app.listen -- /health never answered. check:syntax is a parser and an undefined NAME parses; tsconfig.api.json covers services/api/src and NOT server.js, so `tsc --noEmit | grep server.js(NNNN)` prints nothing for any server.js problem, which reads as a pass and is not one. This checker pulls the identifiers out of every registerXxxRoutes(app, {...}) call and fails if server.js never declares one. Mutation-verified: delete the `function getCurrentUser` line and it reports REGISTER_DEPS_FAILED missing=1 naming the factory, the line and the identifier.
_unit_note: Deterministic, database-free suite. The *-live.test.ts files are OPT-IN, not failing: each is describe.skipIf'd behind RUN_*_LIVE=1 plus a *_API_BASE, so without those they contribute zero evidence while still printing as 'skipped'. That is why they are split out instead of trusted: in the gate they are decoration. `npm run test:live` runs them against a live API and PostgreSQL when someone means it.
_unit_count_pattern: A regex with ONE group capturing how many tests ran. ZERO IS NOT A PASS: a suite that discovered nothing exits 0 and looks perfect. Vitest summarises as `Tests  38 passed (38)` -- or `Tests  3 failed | 35 passed (38)` -- so the group must be anchored on 'passed', not on the first number.
_driver: How the E2E reaches your software. THREE SHAPES cover almost everything:
http     a server. Started on a dynamic port, polled until healthy.
cli      a command. Invoked with args, stdout/stderr asserted.
library  no process at all. The E2E imports and calls it.
A frontend app is `http`, and the agent driving the journeys uses a browser tool. A
rendered window or a game loop is NONE of these -- the logic has to live behind
a headless surface an E2E can drive, and that is an architecture decision to
make before the code exists, not after.
_agent: `.factory/holdout/HOLDOUT.md` are markdown, and this command reads them, uses
the running app, and writes a result file the gate checks.
The prompt arrives on STDIN. Any coding-agent CLI with a headless mode works:
Whatever you put here must be able to RUN A SHELL COMMAND. An agent that can only
edit files cannot use your app, and it will correctly report that it checked
Empty is a FAILURE, not a skip. A gate that quietly drops its end-to-end rung
reports green having never touched the app.
Cost: this runs once per gate, plus once per planted defect during a mutation
run. Point it at a cheaper model than the one writing the code -- the job is
using an app and writing down what happened.

agent._cmd_note: Verified on this machine: codex fails (no `deepseek` provider configured), claude is not logged in, pi works headless -- it reads the prompt on stdin, calls its own tools, and writes files. Cheaper than the model writing the code, which is what this rung wants: the job is using the app and writing down what happened. Local ollama/qwen3.8, so no per-run API cost. Revisit if the journey verdicts read as shallow.

_e2e_timeout_note: The watchdog for the whole agent-driven rung, not a performance budget. 300 s could not cover 4 journeys plus 3 holdout scenarios by an agent that has to read markdown, call the API, and write a result file.

http._start_note: Runs the API only. Journeys that need the web console expect it on http://127.0.0.1:5178 -- start it with `npm run dev:web` before the gate (harness/END-TO-END.md says so in the journey preamble). The API bootstraps runtime DDL and seeds, so boot takes far longer than a toy server.
http._health_contains: A SUBSTRING OF THE RAW BODY, matched literally. services/api/server.js answers /health with {"ok":true,"service":"api","port":N,"status":"ready"}, so 'ready' is the discriminating token -- 'ok' also appears in half the error bodies this API returns.
http._boot_note: Measured: a cold start answers /health in ~95s, because services/api/server.js runs its runtime DDL (dozens of CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) at module load before app.listen. 120s was already marginal and lost the race inside a mutation build. Do not lower this to make the gate feel fast -- a boot timeout is not a performance budget.
http._env: Optional extra environment for the app process. {port} is substituted.

_cli_note: No CLI exists in this repository; the surface is HTTP. An empty command makes the rung SKIP LOUDLY instead of running a Python placeholder that can never start.
_library_note: The repo is ESM ("type": "module"), so require('./') throws ERR_REQUIRE_ESM. The API is a server, not a library: the http driver is the honest shape here.

browser._note: ONLY for an app whose correctness is visual. Leave install_check empty if no journey needs a browser. When it is set, `factory doctor` runs it at setup -- so a missing browser is a setup failure with an install command, not a mystery hang at gate time on a fresh runner.
